neutral_facts.value: The accused, a father, was involved in an incident where his son-in-law, who was an alcoholic, was found dead in his house. The deceased had been staying with the accused's family for several months. The deceased had a history of alcohol abuse and was known to quarrel with his wife and the accused after drinking. The accused's daughter, who was the deceased's wife, stated that her husband was killed by her father. The deceased's brother also reported the incident. Medical evidence indicated fatal injuries to the deceased, and the accused confessed to the act. The trial court convicted the accused of murder, but the High Court and the Supreme Court reconsidered the case, finding that the accused's actions were driven by provocation and loss of self-control, leading to a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The sentence was modified from life imprisonment to ten years rigorous imprisonment.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant was guilty of committing the murder of his son-in-law, based on the evidence including the confession made by the appellant to his daughter and the post-mortem report indicating fatal injuries.

quotes.text: The prosecution examined nine witnesses including the wife of the appellant – Mononit Jajara (P.W.5) and his daughter – Sarani Boria (P.W.6).
The Trial Court on consideration of the above-stated evidence held the appellant guilty of committing an oﬀ ence under Section 302 IPC and consequently, sentenced him to undergo life imprisonment.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no eye witness to the occurrence and that the alleged confession made by the appellant could not be relied upon due to lack of direct evidence.

quotes.text: the defence plea taken by the appellant that there was no eye witness to the occurrence and that the alleged confession made by him before his daughter (P.W.6) could not be relied upon
the defence did not question the two witnesses on the same and not even tried to either controvert or discredit their statement.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle under Exception I of Section 300 IPC, which provides that culpable homicide is not murder if the offender, while deprived of the power of self-control by grave and sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or by mistake or accident.

quotes.text: Exception 1. —When culpable homicide is not murder. — Culpable homicide is not murder if the oﬀ ender, whilst deprived of the power of self-control by grave and sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or causes the death of any other person by mistake or accident.

quotes.text: In our considered opinion, the ends of justice would be adequately met by converting the sentence of life imprisonment awarded to the appellant to rigorous imprisonment of ten years.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court weighed the appellant's motive to prevent his daughter from being harassed by the deceased, the sustained provocation from the deceased's behavior, and the lack of pre-meditation in the act.
